### Devotional: Isaiah 36
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/deut-8-psalm-91-isaiah-36-revelation-6/
Passage: Isaiah 36:1-22
Points:
- Chapters 36–39 serve as the central hinge of Isaiah, posing the vital question of where Judah places its trust.
- Sennacherib’s field commander relies on psychological warfare and half-truths calculated to dismantle faith in God.
- The commander mocks Judah's military helplessness, underscoring the vanity of relying on human allies such as Egypt.
- Assyria deceptively claims divine endorsement, twisting God's providential judgment into supposed personal obedience.
- The enemy frames impending defeat and deportation as pleasant prosperity, masking the bitter reality of subjugation.
- Believers must perceive how worldly and demonic voices still use demoralizing half-truths to shake confidence in God.

### Bible Pathways 08/07/04
Author: Bible Pathways
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-08-or-07-or-04-1277088.html
Passage: Isaiah 36:1
Points:
- Sennacherib swiftly conquered the fortified cities of Judah, leaving Jerusalem seemingly defenseless against a massive empire.
- The Assyrian king sent messengers to demand unconditional surrender and urged the citizens not to trust the Lord's deliverance.
- Spiritual adversaries often use threatening circumstances and boastful intimidation to erode trust in God's power.
- Believers must not rely on human strength against enemy schemes, but instead take every crisis directly to God in prayer.
- God remains sovereign over earth's rulers and faithfully answers those who place their complete dependence upon Him.
